clue.text: Record label tense for release

parts.note: EMI is the famous British record company
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A record company is under pressure to put out a new single.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, so it is a synonym of release.

clue.text: Initially Super Trouper dress is light …

indicators.note: 'Initially' asks for the opening letters of the two words that follow it

parts.note: a robe is a long loose garment, a kind of dress

explanation.surface: Super Trouper is an Abba song and album; its stage gown is said to be lightweight, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 3 Down. A Super Trouper is also a type of big stage spotlight, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a flashing lamp used at discos and concerts, so it is a kind of light.

clue.text: … Agnetha performing in English version of Mamma Mia dress on this?

indicators.note: the shuffled singer's name is placed in the middle of the English exclamation

parts.note: 'Mamma mia!' is an Italian cry of surprise; the British equivalent is 'Cor!'

indicators.note: a performing name is put through its paces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Agnetha Fältskog, one of the two singers in Abba

explanation.surface: Abba singer Agnetha, playing in a British production of Mamma Mia, hangs up her costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mamma mia!' is an Italian cry of surprise; the British equivalent is 'Cor!', like 'blimey'. The ellipsis carries 'dress' on from 2 Down's surface, though here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress is hung on a hanger for storage, so this cryptic phrasing describes the wardrobe item.

clue.text: Record of Abba? Listened out for old song

indicators.note: with the letters out of their places they are free to be rearranged

parts.note: all twenty letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone hears what they think is an Abba record and is listening hard to identify it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listened out' looks like a sound signal, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal. Boiled Beef and Carrots is a Cockney music-hall song from 1909.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of an Edwardian music-hall number, so it is a fair example of an old song.

clue.text: One of us upset getting left inside was once bad

indicators.note: the single letter is placed within the jumbled words, as 'inside' says
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One of our group is upset at being left in prison for having once been wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles ONE OF US to FEONOUS, and L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonous is an archaic word for wicked or criminal, so 'once' marks its age and 'bad' is the meaning.

clue.text: Turn up, initially taking chance on me

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of each of the two words after it

explanation.surface: Take a Chance on Me is an Abba song; here someone hopes a person will show up and gamble on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just links the parts; the song title is broken up so that 'initially' acts on 'chance on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come is to arrive or appear, which is what turning up means as a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Abba song in can following number one?

indicators.note: the toilet word comes after the other, so it is the second half

parts.note: 'number one' is the childish euphemism for urinating, passing water
can is American slang for a toilet, as is loo in Britain

explanation.surface: A joke about singing an Abba hit while sitting on the toilet after a pee.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is the British everyday word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo won Eurovision for Abba in 1974 and became their first big international hit single.

clue.text: Heavenly bodies in type of blood bank

parts.note: O is one of the four main blood groups
RBS is the Royal Bank of Scotland

explanation.surface: Talk of celestial objects stored in a blood bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blood bank' looks like one unit, but it splits into a blood group and a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Orb is a poetic word for a planet, sun or star, a sphere moving through the sky.

clue.text: Newspaper and music magazine once featuring old timer

parts.note: Metro is a free British daily newspaper

indicators.note: the magazine features, so contains, the single letter for old

parts.note: NME (New Musical Express) was a British music weekly, now no longer in print

explanation.surface: A newspaper and a former music weekly both run a feature on an aged ticker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old timer' reads as an elderly person, but 'old' gives O and only 'timer' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome is a clicking device that keeps time for musicians, so it is a kind of timer.

clue.text: Playing song live

parts.note: a show that is on is playing
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A band is performing a song in front of an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being broadcast as it happens, which is the broadcasting sense of live.

clue.text: French all lining river to get fish

indicators.note: the French word lines, so surrounds, the single letter for river

parts.note: tout is French for all

explanation.surface: Every French angler is along the riverbank hoping for a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Promiscuity of Miss getting over love with head

indicators.note: the word for miss gets on either side of, so wraps, the letter for love

parts.note: to miss something is to lose it
O is love, a zero score in tennis
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A young woman's sleeping around becomes the topic once she gets over a lost love.
explanation.definitionFit: Looseness in old-fashioned usage means sexual laxity, a synonym for promiscuity.

clue.text: See 4
Music tones

definitions.meaning: a genre of music rooted in African-American folk song
shades or hues of the colour blue

explanation.surface: A two-word note about musical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Blues is both a melancholy musical style and the plural of a colour, so both senses apply.

clue.text: Wise people round learner driver cutting speeds

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the learner letter cuts into the word for speeds

parts.note: to race is to speed
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: Clever folk hover around a learner who keeps breaking the speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: RACES is split RAC-ES by L.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles are people regarded as sources of wise counsel, from the prophets of ancient Greece.

clue.text: 16 to follow as lights roam around

definitions.note: 16 Down is STEPS, so the definition is 'steps to follow'

indicators.note: the letters roam around and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Following the band Steps as stage lights swirl around.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a set of instructions, a sequence of steps carried out in order.

clue.text: Group from Sweden: time to go over records

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits above, over, the second

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: A group from Sweden, like Abba, revisits its back catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Steps is a British pop group of the late 1990s who were known for Abba covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps is a five-piece pop act, so it is an example of a musical group.

clue.text: Remove clip from one page, say

parts.note: un is French for one
e.g. (for example) means say

explanation.surface: Instructions for taking a paperclip off a single sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg is to take out a peg, the clip that holds something fixed, such as washing.

clue.text: Dancing Queen apt or The Name of the Game?

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing between two Abba songs, Dancing Queen and The Name of the Game.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read literally: what the game is called. 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pétanque is a French bowls game, so its name is literally the name of a game.

clue.text: Abba song mostly average

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the synonym

parts.note: so-so means average or middling

explanation.surface: A verdict that an Abba song is mostly mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: SOS was an Abba single of 1975, named for the Morse distress call.

clue.text: Woman has sex with affairs

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
bangs is vulgar slang for has sex

explanation.surface: A woman has flings with various lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affairs' looks romantic but means things in general, as in the whole shebang.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebang is a matter or business, as in 'the whole shebang', so shebangs are affairs.

clue.text: Handy protection's good before passion

indicators.note: the single letter comes before the other word in the answer

parts.note: love is passion

explanation.surface: A wink at contraception: being careful before passion is a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' means for the hand, not convenient. The 's is a contraction of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove is a covering worn to protect the hand.

clue.text: Release songs for performance without payment

parts.note: a set is the list of songs a band plays at a gig
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A band offers its gig songs at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to liberate, the same as releasing someone.

clue.text: See 4
Pet fish died: bowl terrible, ultimately

parts.note: the cod is a sea fish
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died

indicators.note: 'ultimately' asks for the final letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A pet goldfish has died because its bowl was dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle someone is to pamper them, the same as petting in its sense of indulging.

clue.text: Exaggerate, having finished act

parts.note: something over is finished
to do is to act

explanation.surface: A performer hams it up once the show is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it too far, which is what exaggerating means.

clue.text: Crowd get up where musicians play

parts.note: a band is a group or crowd of people
to stand is to get up

explanation.surface: A crowd rises to its feet at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandstand is an outdoor platform, often in a park, for musical performances.

clue.text: Hit poor piano

parts.note: bum is slang for poor or worthless, as in a bum note
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Striking a badly made piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a knock or collision, so to bump is to hit.

clue.text: Face party

definitions.meaning: a face of a solid, such as one face of a cube
one party in a dispute or match

explanation.surface: Two words that read as facing a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Side is both a surface of an object and a team or faction, so it fits both senses.

clue.text: Rows from couples: right to break up?

indicators.note: the letter for right breaks up the word, sitting in its middle

parts.note: to tie is to couple or join together

explanation.surface: Couples arguing over whether it is right to split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels to go with 'break up'; it means lines of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows or layers set one above another, as in a stadium.

clue.text: So Long, half cut single

indicators.note: half the word is cut away, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: So Long is an Abba song; a cut-down version is released as a single.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo means alone or by oneself, a synonym for single.

clue.text: Pile of money, money, money — small amount dropped off

indicators.note: dropped off means the coin letter is removed from the currency word

parts.note: the pound is the British unit of money
P is a penny, a small amount of British money

explanation.surface: Money, Money, Money is an Abba song; a heap of cash with a little falling away.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound is a heap or pile of earth or other material.

clue.text: The Winner Takes It All demo good: Ring, Ring going to get remixed

indicators.note: a remix is a reworking of a track, so the letters are rearranged
going means leaving, so the two rings are taken out of the word

parts.note: each ring is O, the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: Abba songs The Winner Takes It All and Ring, Ring set to be remixed from a good demo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' takes OO out of GOOD, leaving GD; 'to get remixed' shuffles ALL DEMO GD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold medal is the prize awarded to the first-place finisher, which only the champion receives.
